units.translation: Unutterable with gentle rites: he means the rites performed in Samothrace, which if anyone is initiated into, he is preserved in storms at sea. And they say that Odysseus, having been initiated in Samothrace, used the veil instead of a fillet (ε 346); for around the belly the initiated fasten purple fillets. And they say that Agamemnon, having been initiated, when he was in great confusion at Troy, stopped the disorder of the Greeks by holding a purple cloth (Θ 221). They are initiated in Samothrace to the Cabeiri, as Mnaseas (fg 27 M. III 154) says. And their names are four in number: Axieros,

Axiokersa, Axiokersos, 〈Kasmilos〉. Axieros then is Demeter, Axiokersa is Persephone, Axiokersos is Hades; and the fourth added, Kasmilos, is Hermes, as Dionysodorus (68 fg 1 J.) relates. The Cabeiri seem to be named from the Cabeirian mountains in Phrygia, since they were brought from there. Others say that the Cabeiri are two, the elder Zeus, the younger Dionysus.

Samothrace was formerly called Leucosia, as Aristotle relates in the Constitution of Samothrace (fg 538 Rose 1567a 34). Later, from Saos, the son of Hermes and Rhene, it was renamed Samos by insertion of the m. When Thracians settled it, it was called Samothrace.
